theme: Threads, run loops and dispatch barriers

terms.definition: A single path of execution inside a process, where code runs one step at a time.
terms.example: Each thread runs its own steps in order.

terms.definition: A loop that waits for events such as timers and input, then runs the work for each one.
terms.example: The run loop wakes up when an event arrives.
terms.code:
import Foundation
let loop = RunLoop.current
loop.perform { print("handled event") }
loop.run(until: Date(timeIntervalSinceNow: 0.1))

terms.definition: A task on a concurrent queue that waits for earlier tasks, runs alone, then lets later tasks start.
terms.example: Wrap every write in a dispatch barrier.

video.title: Thread, Run Loop & Dispatch Barrier | Day 254
video.description:
Learn to explain where code runs and how to protect a shared cache: Thread, Run Loop & Dispatch Barrier, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Thread - A single path of execution inside a process, where code runs one step at a time.
Run Loop - A loop that waits for events such as timers and input, then runs the work for each one.
Dispatch Barrier - A task on a concurrent queue that waits for earlier tasks, runs alone, then lets later tasks start.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.description:
Explain Thread, Run Loop & Dispatch Barrier in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Thread, Run Loop, Dispatch Barrier 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Thread - A single path of execution inside a process, where code runs one step at a time.
한국어: Thread: 프로세스 안에서 코드를 한 단계씩 실행하는 하나의 실행 경로

Run Loop - A loop that waits for events such as timers and input, then runs the work for each one.
한국어: Run Loop: 타이머나 입력 같은 이벤트를 기다렸다가 각각의 작업을 실행하는 반복 구조

Dispatch Barrier - A task on a concurrent queue that waits for earlier tasks, runs alone, then lets later tasks start.
한국어: Dispatch Barrier: 동시 큐에서 앞선 작업을 기다린 뒤 혼자 실행되고 그다음 작업을 시작시키는 작업

landscape.hook: Can you explain Thread, Run Loop and Dispatch Barrier in English?

dialogue.title: The shared cache
dialogue.setting: A cache with many readers and one writer

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I read the cache from many places, but I also write to it sometimes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then keep the cache behind a concurrent queue and use a dispatch barrier for writes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What does a dispatch barrier do?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It waits for earlier tasks, runs alone, and then lets later tasks start.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Does it start a new thread for the write?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. A thread is a path where code runs one step at a time, and the queue chooses it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I see. And what is the run loop in my app?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A run loop waits for events like timers and touches, and then runs the work for each event.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can I write to `cache` from the run loop?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, but still use a dispatch barrier. Reads on another thread may happen at the same time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Okay, I will wrap every write in a dispatch barrier.
Each thread runs its own steps in order.
